import pandas as pd
from collections import Counter
import re
xl = "/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/9b54f9d9-35ee-4a14-b62f-d130ea00317f_extracted/food_duplicates.xls"
df = pd.read_excel(xl)
vals = [str(x).strip().lower() for x in df.values.flatten() if pd.notnull(x) and str(x).strip()!='']
# Basic canonicalization
canon = lambda s: re.sub(r"[^a-z]+"," ",s).strip()
vals_c = [canon(v) for v in vals]
# Known synonym clusters (subset)
syn_groups = [
  {"aubergine","eggplant"},
  {"courgette","zucchini"},
  {"cilantro","coriander"},
  {"garbanzo bean","chickpea"},
  {"soda","pop"},
  {"sultana","golden raisin"},
  {"cotton candy","candy floss"},
  {"beet","beetroot"},
  {"congee","rice porridge"},
  {"flapjack","pancake"},
]
valset = set(vals_c)
# Mark covered items (those having a partner)
covered = set()
for g in syn_groups:
    if g.issubset(valset):
        covered |= g
# Candidates that appear once and are not covered by synonym pairs
cnt = Counter(vals_c)
singletons = {k for k,v in cnt.items() if v==1}
unique_candidates = list(singletons - covered)
# Focus on items with distinctive heads likely to be mapped to categories
cands = [c for c in unique_candidates if c in {"turtle soup","hoagie","pancake","flapjack"}]
print("Candidate unique items:", sorted(set(cands)))
